title: Ask or Answer: A Decision Framework for Multi-Turn Health Misinformation Intervention
abstract: arXiv:2608.21721v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Correcting health misinformation in dialogue requires more than producing a factual rebuttal: users differ in what they know, what they believe, and what they need to hear, so an effective intervention often depends on first asking the right clarifying question. Yet existing methods either respond immediately or probe indiscriminately, treating clarification as either unnecessary or always beneficial. We propose Reward-Optimized Probe-and-Respond (RO-PnR), a framework that learns when asking is worth its cost. At each turn, RO-PnR chooses between probing for more information and committing to a final correction, guided by a turn-level reward that weighs the expected gain from probing against its interaction cost. To capture how user heterogeneity affects probing value, we model each simulated user with a latent state along health literacy and belief commitment. translated_title: 提问还是回答：多轮健康 misinformation 干预的决策框架
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.21721v1 公告类型：新 摘要：在对话中纠正健康 misinformation 不仅仅需要提供事实性反驳：用户的知识、信念和需求各不相同，因此有效的干预往往首先依赖于提出正确的澄清问题。然而，现有方法要么立即回应，要么不加区分地进行探查，将澄清视为要么不必要，要么总是有益。我们提出奖励优化的探查-回应（RO-PnR）框架，该框架学习何时提问值得其成本。在每一轮中，RO-PnR 在探查更多信息和承诺最终纠正之间进行选择，由一轮级奖励引导，该奖励权衡探查的预期收益与其交互成本。为了捕捉用户异质性对探查价值的影响，我们为每个模拟用户建模一个潜在状态，涵盖健康素养和信念承诺。实验表明，RO-PnR 在成本调整效用上实现了最高值。
tldr: RO-PnR 框架通过学习在提问与回应之间做出最优权衡，显著提升了多轮健康 misinformation 干预的成本调整效用。
en_tdlr: The RO-PnR framework learns to optimally trade off between probing and responding, significantly improving cost-adjusted utility in multi-turn health misinformation intervention.
